referents.why: Second masculine singular possessive on hand in cl2, a command inside the quoted speech that Moses is to say. That speech is addressed to Aaron (w7), the only masculine singular addressee it has. Agrees with the builder.
Second masculine singular possessive on staff in the same command in cl2; same speech, same addressee, Aaron (w7). Agrees with the builder.

The implied you of cl1 (say to Aaron) is the one LORD speaks to in cl0, Moses (w4). cl1 is the command given to Moses; Aaron is the addressee of the speech Moses is told to give, not the subject of cl1. The builder's w7 is wrong here.
The implied you of cl2 is inside the quoted words that cl1 introduces. Those words are addressed to Aaron (w7), as cl1 names him, so the morphology and the speech both fix Aaron.
referents.category: implied subject inside a commanded speech

referents.why: The implied you of cl3 is a further command in the same quoted speech as cl2, joined to it by a plain waw at one level, so it shares cl2's addressee, Aaron (w7).
referents.category: implied subject inside a commanded speech

links.why: Plain waw joining two second-person commands at one level. The and type is what the form gives, and both clauses belong to one imperative group. Not a result (no third-person weqatal) and not a purpose (no change of person).
cl0 he said Yahweh to Moses introduces the words Tell Aaron, which are the command cl1. The speech clause's content is that clause.
cl1 say to Aaron introduces the quoted commands cl2 and cl3. Commands joined by and at one level are the content as a whole, so the content link goes to the imperative group, not to cl2 alone.

groups.why: LORD (w2) speaks (cl0) to Moses (w4). The commanded turn is nested as the part. The builder listed cl1, cl2 and cl3 directly as parts, but cl2 and cl3 are said by Moses to Aaron, inside the command to say, so they sit one level down in turn1.

Moses (w4) says to Aaron (w7) what cl1 commands him to say. The builder gave the sender as the slot cl1s; the sender must be a candidate, and the one who speaks is Moses. What is said is the imperative group imp2.
Two second-person commands joined by a plain waw at one level form one imperative group. The builder held cl3 as a part, but it is a command. No effect is stated in this verse.

none_fit.what: The sense is that stretching out the staff brings about the frogs. The result type needs a third-person weqatal after the command, and the and type is only a plain waw, so neither states this two-command outcome.

cant_tell.what: Whether cl3 (bring up the frogs) is the effect of the imperative group imp2, that is, what the stretching is meant to bring about.
cant_tell.why: This verse has no weqatal after the commands, so the effect is not stated here. It may be stated, or only implied, in a later verse.
